Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserve.
Asset type: original game character sheet for Request 22, landscape 1536x1024.
Input image 1 is the ADOPTED PROTAGONIST SHEET and the EDIT TARGET. Preserve it exactly outside the backpack hardware and its camera. Keep the same man's face, curls, warm tan complexion, age, slim athletic adult proportions, amber prescription glasses, dark respirator with orange filter rings, dark teal zip work jacket with orange collar lining and details, plain grey tee, charcoal cargo pants, brown work boots, poses, sheet composition, lighting, blue-grey background and clean stylized sculpted rendering. Do not redesign him.
Change ONLY his backpack, its straps where attachment requires it, and add its 360-degree camera. The pack is a portable real computer with batteries and cooling, backpack shaped and wearable, NOT a cloth bag. Replace the olive fabric pack in every view with a COMPACT NEWER RUGGED INDUSTRIAL COMPUTER: smooth moulded graphite/olive-grey hard shell with clean curved corners, a properly integrated dark vent grille, tidy protected cable runs and one restrained orange hardware detail. Practical slightly futuristic premium hardware visually close to today's industrial equipment, not science-fiction armor. Maintain similar overall pack size and position, believable dark shoulder harness. The tradesman is an electrician whose family can afford good hardware; compact, well installed and orderly.
Add ONE short sturdy camera mast mounted on the pack's upper corner, rising just above his shoulder/head line to provide an unobstructed 360-degree view. Offset it slightly behind the shoulder so its outline is visible from the front as well as back and elevated views. The camera is a SMALL BLACK CYLINDRICAL SENSOR RING with multiple tiny outward lenses or a small omnidirectional dome, not a face, head or glowing eye. Keep its scale modest, sturdy protected mast and neat wiring; same single mast and sensor design in all body views. Do not alter the unmasked portrait except for any existing cropped harness naturally implied.
LOCK the original four-view layout and crop exactly: masked FRONT full body on left, BACK full body in center, unmasked head-and-shoulders portrait upper right, elevated rear three-quarter 50-degree battle-camera view lower right; identical view sizes and framing. Entire heads and shoes visible. Soft neutral studio light, smooth broad matte material shading, crisp authored fold planes, subtly exaggerated adult game-character proportions identical to the input. No additional views, equipment or character.
Avoid: cloth backpack, zippers on the shell, pockets, screen, display, artificial face, luminous sensor, neon, armor, white-and-red palette, text, captions, logos, emblems, brand marks, watermark. Output ONE sheet of the same protagonist with only the revised computer and visible 360 camera.

Use case: stylized-concept / identity-preserve character redesign.
Asset type: original game WRITER character turnaround sheet for Request 22, landscape 1536x1024.
INPUT IMAGE 1: adopted STYLE, LIGHTING and FOUR-VIEW LAYOUT reference only. Match its clean sculpted stylized adult game-character rendering, broad smooth material shading, expressive designed facial planes, slightly enlarged head/hands, restrained texture, crisp cloth folds and plain blue-grey background exactly. Do not copy the man's outfit or face.
INPUT IMAGE 2: FACE AND HAIR reference only. Use the woman's feminine oval face shape, defined cheekbones, strong arched eyebrows, almond-shaped eyes, full lips and abundant long natural dark curls as the basis for a stylized ORIGINAL character. Do not copy her clothing, jewelry, runway context, bright pink sweater, black skirt, handbag or makeup styling. The character has DEEP DARK BROWN SKIN, rich espresso/chocolate brown with controlled warm highlights, consistently in all views.
INPUT IMAGE 3: previous writer sheet, for her identity/accessories and rendering context; replace her short hair, hoodie, jeans, sneakers and cloth pack according to this revision.
Subject: Black woman early 30s, feminine lean adult build and poised relaxed stance, clearly a woman and distinct from both men. A broke former journalist who now writes and prints illegal resistance newspapers in a California city around 2046. Contemporary secondhand civilian clothing; cool and thoughtful, no tactical uniform or futuristic costume.
HAIR: substantial black natural curls that fall PAST HER SHOULDERS when unmasked, matching the long curly reference. Show this long free hairstyle in the upper-right portrait. In the front/back/elevated masked body views, the same long hair is tied back in a loose practical low curly ponytail, exposing the glasses and keeping the pack camera unobstructed. The ponytail's curls extend past her shoulders; do not make a bob or short crop.
KEEP her large round bronze glasses with hinged ROUND flip-up infrared filters raised above the prescription lenses in every view. Her deep MAGENTA BANDANA covers nose and mouth in the full-body and battle-camera views, and is down at the neck in the unmasked portrait. Keep small subtle ink smudges on a few fingers.
OUTFIT, approved direction: a long secondhand coat, MID-CALF or at least knee length, charcoal-brown neutral with worn cuffs and one modest tonal repair, slightly shaped at the waist, open below the waist for movement. Beneath it, thrifted layers: a plain faded warm-grey knit top and a casually draped muted plum scarf, simple slim dark trousers and worn lace-up ankle boots. A long coat gives her a slim, flowing vertical silhouette unlike either man's short top. Civilian streetwear with personality, elegant through shape rather than expensive fashion. Subtle magenta on the bandana and one small incidental scarf detail; never a color-swapped team uniform. No decorative jewelry from the photo.
PACK: a CHEAP OLD SECONDHAND CONSUMER COMPUTER worn as a backpack, NOT fabric: a smaller faded taupe-grey/yellowed plastic hard case with rounded dated consumer-product shape, real dark cooling grille, one mismatched replacement plastic panel, scuffed corners, a cracked corner patched with dark tape. Believable battery and cooling, dark load-bearing straps. A folded newspaper tucked under one strap. No words printed on the paper.
CAMERA: ONE thin mast from an upper pack corner, slightly crooked but securely attached using tape and zip ties, extending behind the shoulder to just above the head line. Small black cylindrical 360-degree camera ring with tiny outward lenses/dome, visible in every full-body view including front and overhead. Same design and mounting in each view. A working sensor, not a robot head/face/eye; no screen or glow.
COMPOSITION: replicate input 1 exactly: masked FRONT full-body left, BACK full-body center, large unmasked head-and-shoulders portrait top right, smaller elevated rear three-quarter full-body battle-camera view bottom right at roughly 50 degrees. Consistent same woman, coat, long hair, mask/glasses, computer case and camera in all views, same full-body scale and spacing, complete crown and shoes. Portrait should clearly communicate the photo-inspired feminine face and long loose curls, glasses retained, bandana down.
Soft neutral studio light, smooth clean stylized sculpted surfaces and adult proportions from input 1, no photographic microtextures, anime eyes or painterly grain. Avoid: short hair, hoodie/jeans outfit, cropped jacket, glamour/runway costume, fabric backpack, screen, artificial face, glowing eye, neon, armor, white-and-red palette, captions, text, logo, emblem, brand mark, watermark. ONE four-view sheet.

Use case: identity-preserve / outfit and equipment redesign.
Asset type: original game DEVELOPER character sheet for Request 22, landscape 1536x1024.
Input image 1 is the adopted STYLE / LIGHTING / LAYOUT reference ONLY. Match its clean sculpted stylized adult game-character rendering and blue-grey studio setting exactly; do not copy the protagonist's face or fitted zip jacket.
Input image 2 is the DEVELOPER EDIT TARGET and locks the identity: identical light-skinned heavyset mid-40s man with comfortable belly and broad shoulders, friendly round face, warm slight smile, thinning/receding brown-grey hair with crown showing, short greying beard and rectangular dark glasses. Keep his age, face, complexion, hair, beard, body size, glasses, warmth and four-view layout. Keep the quiet muted pine-green neck gaiter, ordinary matte cloth, pulled over nose/mouth in body views and down around neck in the portrait; do not brighten it.
Redesign his outfit and pack only. The character is a former senior software engineer, laid off after AI took knowledge jobs, a warm unflashy dad presence and an old-school hacker. California around 2046, visibly contemporary shabby civilian clothes, no armor, neon or futuristic fabric.
OUTFIT: a worn CHARCOAL PADDED SLEEVELESS VEST, with a few broad horizontal quilted sections, over a long-sleeved muted brown-grey FLANNEL SHIRT with a subdued broad check, cuffs casually pushed up just a little. Vest open naturally over his belly; plain dark tee underneath if visible. Replace the cardigan completely. The vest defines a broad solid rounded torso, flannel sleeves distinct beside it, unlike the protagonist's fitted jacket and the writer's long coat. Faded dark work pants, relaxed ordinary fit without bulky tactical cargo pouches; comfortable worn brown TRAIL SHOES with modest robust soles. No uniform matching colored trim. Muted terminal/pine green stays on the gaiter and at most a tiny incidental detail. A short cable coil secured on a pack strap is his one nod to old-school hacking; no lanyard needed.
PACK: the largest and heaviest of the three, a HOMEMADE OPEN-FRAME WEARABLE COMPUTER assembled from salvaged SERVER PARTS. A compact rectangular exposed dark metal frame, visible vertical aluminium heat-sink fins and ONE visible round cooling fan, inset battery/compute boxes, old latches, clearly hand-routed protected cable bundles tied to the frame. Purposeful messy hand-built industrial hardware, credible rigid backpack-scale computer rather than a cloth bag or futuristic weapon. A couple of worn plain sticker remnants with no readable writing, logos or symbols. Dark sturdy load-bearing harness and realistic straps. Distinct open frame silhouette and finned edges, not a smooth molded case or olive fabric pouch.
CAMERA: ONE salvaged small cylindrical 360-degree sensor ring/dome on a jury-rigged ARTICULATED METAL ARM with one clear hinge and tied cable, bolted to the upper frame. Arm reaches behind the shoulder to just above head level, offset so the small camera silhouette is visible from front, back and elevated angles. Same sensor/arm construction and mounting in every body view. Four tiny outward lenses or an omnidirectional dome; the sensor is a practical camera, not a head, face or glowing eye.
LOCK the four-view composition to input 2: full-body masked FRONT left, BACK center at same scale, unmasked head-and-shoulders portrait upper right, smaller 50-degree elevated rear three-quarter full-body battle-camera view bottom right. Same poses/spacing and fully visible heads/shoes. Update shirt/vest/pack/camera consistently across all four views, retain the man's face exactly in the portrait. Plain blue-grey background, soft neutral studio light, broad smooth clean material shading, designed expressive facial planes, crisp stylized fabric folds, identical adopted character style.
Avoid: slender body, changing face or age, bright mint gaiter, cardigan, leather jacket, uniform, fabric backpack, sealed molded pack, display, screen, luminous parts, artificial face, robot head, white-and-red palette, sci-fi armor, words, captions, logos, brand marks, watermark. Output ONE sheet of the same heavyset developer in the vest/flannel/work pants/trail shoes with a homemade server computer and articulated 360 camera.

Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserve.

Deepen all exposed skin to rich dark chocolate/espresso brown: a base around #4E2F25 with restrained warm brown highlights around #79503B. Natural dark brown skin with dimensional clean studio shading, not orange, bronze, yellow or light tan. Apply this consistently to the unmasked portrait's face/ears/neck, the masked full-body forehead/face/ears/neck, both full-body forearms/hands/fingers, and the exposed skin in the elevated view. Preserve facial features and facial shading geometry; change the complexion, not the person's face, age, expression, build or ethnicity.
Every other pixel and design is locked: identical feminine almond eyes, defined cheekbones, expressive brows/full lips, long black curls free past shoulders in portrait and tied back in body views; round bronze glasses with raised round flip-up infrared filters; magenta mask and muted plum scarf; long charcoal-brown worn coat with the same length, damage, patches and folds; warm-grey knit layer, slim trousers, ankle boots, ink on fingers; faded tan plastic secondhand computer with cooling grille, taped crack, paper under strap and thin taped 360 camera stalk. Same cameras and poses, exact same 1536x1024 four-view layout, unmasked portrait top right, masked front/back full-body left/center, elevated rear view lower right, identical blue-grey background and clean stylized material rendering.
Do not redesign, darken or recolor any garment, hair, glasses, computer, camera or backdrop. No added details, captions, text, logos or watermark. Output the same sheet with only the requested deep brown complexion corrected.

Use case: stylized-concept / reference-preserving product turnaround.
Asset type: ONE landscape 1536x1024 standalone pack lineup for original game Request 22.
Input images 1, 2, 3 are the FINISHED character sheets. Extract and preserve the EXACT wearable computer and 360-camera designs shown on their backs, using the back and elevated views as the references. They control geometry, panel shape, vent arrangement, camera design and mounting, cables, repair details, materials, colors, relative scale and clean stylized rendering. Show their HARDWARE ONLY, with no people, head, body or clothing. Do not invent alternative pack designs or generic fabric bags.
Scene: plain BLUE-GREY studio backdrop matching the sheets, soft neutral lighting, minimal soft contact shading. Clean sculpted stylized game-asset presentation, broad smooth material shading and restrained wear matching the input sheets.
COMPOSITION: exactly THREE COLUMNS and TWO ROWS, comfortably spaced, every whole pack and raised mast completely in frame. Left column = protagonist's newer industrial computer from image 1. Middle column = writer's old consumer computer from image 2. Right column = developer's homemade server computer from image 3. TOP ROW = straight-on BACK/OUTSIDE view of each unit, matching the character back views. BOTTOM ROW = rear THREE-QUARTER view of that exact same unit, rotated to reveal its depth, back, side and dark shoulder harness on the body-facing side. Six pack depictions total; each column contains the same single design in its two views. All six views at the SAME PHYSICAL SCALE: writer slightly smaller than protagonist, developer larger/heavier. Keep the cases backpack-sized and wearable. Top row aligned around case bases, bottom row likewise. No captions or labels; order communicated by arrangement.
LEFT / PROTAGONIST: preserve the compact newer premium moulded GRAPHITE/OLIVE-GREY rugged shell from image 1, curved corners, dark rectangular central vent and two smaller lower-side vents, clean flush panels, integrated handle, dark padded harness and one narrow orange side hardware piece, neatly protected cable run. Same sturdy SHORT telescoping camera mast mounted on the upper side shown in image 1, small black cylindrical omnidirectional camera ring with tiny outward lenses, tidy orange cable detail. Newer durable industrial equipment with only light wear.
MIDDLE / WRITER: preserve the dated faded TAUPE/YELLOWED PLASTIC rectangular consumer shell from image 2, rounded corner case, central dark cooling grille, small mismatched replacement panel, scuffs, taped cracked upper corner, worn dark harness and folded newspaper held under the side strap. Camera remains the same THIN SLIGHTLY CROOKED POLE secured with tape and zip ties, small cylindrical sensor ring at the top, uneven black cable. Old but functional, consumer product repaired to keep working. Plain newspaper folds, no readable printed writing.
RIGHT / DEVELOPER: preserve the exposed DARK METAL OPEN FRAME server rig from image 3, tall vertical aluminum heat-sink fins on one half, one clearly visible ROUND COOLING FAN on the other half, inset compute/battery boxes, old latches, plain faded sticker remnants, tied hand-routed black/red/orange cable bundles and sturdy dark load-bearing harness. Largest/heaviest, open edges and exposed fins, same improvised articulated hinged METAL CAMERA ARM on its upper side, same small black cylindrical multi-lens omnidirectional camera. No screen or elaborate weapon styling.
Cameras: every mast/arm is raised in every view. Match the SMALL sensor shapes to each sheet, distributed 360 lenses/dome, no robot head, face, mascot or glowing eye. Exactly ONE mast/camera per pack depiction. Keep all the same mounting sides relative to each pack as in its reference, naturally transformed for the three-quarter angle.
Avoid: people, mannequin, human silhouette, clothing, cloth pack shell, futuristic armor, extra pack variants or equipment, digital display, screen, face, glow, neon, branding, logo, emblem, captions, labels, text, watermark, cropped cameras or straps. ONE image showing the three EXISTING computer packs faithfully in back and three-quarter views.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, a finished four-view protagonist sheet. Make ONE localized geometrical correction in the LEFTMOST FRONT full-body panel ONLY.
In the middle BACK panel, the 360 camera mast is on the character's anatomical LEFT shoulder (viewer LEFT when looking at his back). Therefore in the FRONT panel it must be on viewer RIGHT, the character's same anatomical LEFT shoulder. The current front sensor is incorrectly on viewer LEFT.
Move only the FRONT-panel camera sensor, complete short sturdy black mast, orange cable and its attachment from viewer LEFT of his head to viewer RIGHT of his head. Place it behind his viewer-RIGHT shoulder, outside the head silhouette, keeping the same mast height, ring-camera shape, diameter, lens arrangement, materials, cable details and plausible connection to the pack. Restore the small old camera area on viewer LEFT to the plain background and original shoulder/harness appearance. Keep the FRONT man's face, hair, respirator, glasses, jacket, orange collar trim, straps, body, hands and pose exactly unchanged.
ABSOLUTELY LOCK the other THREE PANELS: the middle BACK view and its pack/mast, upper-right unmasked portrait, lower-right elevated view and its pack/mast. No changes to them at all. Also lock all framing, background, light, colors, dimensions (1536x1024), clothing folds, shoes, face and the hard-shell industrial pack. Preserve all other pixels. No mirroring of the character or sheet. No added views, text, logos, or new hardware.
Output the SAME sheet, with only the FRONT camera correctly located on viewer RIGHT so front/back mounting agrees anatomically.
